A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SKS framework for nonlinear PDEs. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original solution-error and runtime experiments across four PDE families, including appendix studies of grid shape, irregular domains, and hyperparameter sensitivity.

after.justification: v4 retains these empirical results and adds comparisons involving coefficient optimization, DAKS sampling, and computation without Kronecker acceleration.

M1.justification: The kernel interpolant, optimization over solution values, RKHS/residual objective, and product-kernel Kronecker computation are retained. The added coefficient and full-matrix variants are comparison experiments; the proposed solver is unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Burgers, nonlinear elliptic, Eikonal, and Allen-Cahn cases, including the circular and triangular domains. The added experiments use existing PDE scenarios.

E2.justification: DAKS, PINN, and finite-difference comparisons remain. v4 adds SKS-Naive to the runtime comparison in Table 9 and a coefficient-optimized variant against the proposed parameterization in Table 10.

E3.justification: v4 adds matched-grid DAKS testing and controlled coefficient/full-matrix comparisons. Existing benchmark metrics and budgets are retained. Table 2 now references Table 1a's grids, conflicting with the retained 3:1 Burgers grid description; this reporting inconsistency does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The diagnostic evidence expands substantially: Table 9 isolates Kronecker acceleration, C.5/Table 10 quantifies the previously asserted disadvantage of coefficient optimization, and C.6/Table 11 tests whether DAKS benefits from SKS's regular grids. These address computational attribution, parameterization, and comparison fairness beyond the retained sensitivity studies.

E5.justification: Both versions report DAKS averages over ten randomly sampled collocation sets. v4 adds no new seed counts, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 1–8 and existing Table 9 results are unchanged. Added results include coefficient-optimization error of 1.56E-03 versus 7.83E-04 for solution-value optimization at 2400 points, and grid-DAKS error of 5.67E-02 versus 9.76E-05 for random sampling at 4800 points. New runtime entries quantify SKS-Naive's overhead.

T1.justification: Lemma 4.2 adds a uniformly bounded Voronoi-cell aspect-ratio assumption. Appendix A makes the partition explicit and restores the cell-volume factor in the constant-function norm, changing h^(2k) to h^(2k+d) in the corresponding residual term. The final convergence rate and Proposition 4.3 are retained.

C1.justification: The framework, scalability, convergence, and accuracy contributions remain. The conclusion modestly qualifies the assertion that massive collocation sets are 'necessary for challenging PDEs' to saying they 'can be important for solving challenging PDEs.'

C2.justification: v4 expands the coefficient-optimization explanation to global coefficient influence and conflicts between boundary fitting and residual minimization. It also explains why blockwise Kronecker structure in DAKS does not provide SKS's whole-matrix acceleration. The optimization limitations in Appendix D remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 announces an implementation release and supplies a repository link. It newly documents the 1000-update stopping criterion, alpha/beta search range, and staged random/grid hyperparameter search. These are documentation additions; the PDFs do not establish changes to the existing experiments.

R1.justification: v4 adds Long et al.'s AutoIP and targeted RBF references. Its revised RBF discussion acknowledges residual-minimization methods and local nodal interpolation, qualifying v1's optimization-versus-linear-system distinction. The broader positioning against derivative-augmented kernel solvers remains.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include a focused RBF rewrite, expanded implementation and interpretation passages, new appendix subsections C.5–C.6, and acknowledgments and an impact statement.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch from a single-column preprint to a two-column conference layout, with extensively reformatted tables. v4 adds a fill-distance plot displaying the retained resolution/error trend, Tables 10–11, and runtime rows; existing heatmaps are enlarged and regrouped.

improvement.justification: v4 improves reproducibility, clarifies theoretical assumptions, and supplies useful controls for previously weakly supported design explanations. The gains are limited by new reporting problems: Tables 9–10 support roughly 30–61-fold runtime differences and 2–5-fold coefficient-error differences, below the accompanying claims, and Table 2 introduces a grid-description inconsistency. The retained benchmark evidence and main conclusions remain stable.
